ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, D and E are points on AB and AC, respectively. AF bisects $\angle BAC$ and intersects DE at point G and intersects BC at point F. If $\angle AED=\angle B$, and $AG: GF=3:2$, what is the ratio of $DE: BC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that $\angle DAE = \angle CAB$ and $\angle AED = \angle B$,\\
it follows that $\triangle ADE \sim \triangle ACB$,\\
since $GA$ and $FA$ are the angle bisectors of $\triangle ADE$ and $\triangle ABC$ respectively,\\
therefore $\frac{DE}{BC} = \frac{AG}{AF}$ (the ratio of the corresponding angle bisectors is equal to the similarity ratio),\\
$AG:FG = 3:2$,\\
thus, $AG:AF = 3:5$,\\
hence, $DE:BC = \boxed{3:5}$.
